family: Orders ended by a class-wide event: NIRA Title I orders (X1 type nra_code_approval), Canal Zone orders (canal_zone) and Philippine orders (philippines)

mechanisms.description: NIRA section 2(c), as amended by section 1 of S.J. Res. 113 (June 14, 1935): Title I 'shall cease to be in effect and any agencies established hereunder shall cease to exist' on April 1, 1936. It ends by its terms every agency established under Title I and the Title under which every Title I order operated.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: Fixed: April 1, 1936 at the latest; an earlier end (own terms, a later order, the June 14, 1935 repeal of code provisions) controls when shown.

mechanisms.description: EO 7076 (June 15, 1935) amended 'all existing Executive Orders heretofore issued under' Title I 'so as to continue them in effect and to extend their operation ... until April 1, 1936', subject to earlier limitation or cancellation and expressly without any code-approval or code-enforcement power. It writes an outer end date into every Title I order issued before June 15, 1935.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: Interval: from the order's date to April 1, 1936.

mechanisms.description: S.J. Res. 113 section 2 (June 14, 1935) repealed every Title I provision 'delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes'. Code-dependent commands ended that day; this falls inside the M1/M2 interval and is not used as a separate date by this doctrine.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: Fixed: June 14, 1935, for code-dependent commands only.

mechanisms.description: Schechter Poultry Corp. v. United States (May 27, 1935) and Panama Refining Co. v. Ryan (January 7, 1935) held the section 3 code-making delegation and the section 9(c) petroleum delegation unconstitutional. They are recorded as validity characterizations, not end dates; no branch dates an end by them.
EO 7075 section 1 (June 15, 1935): 'The National Industrial Recovery Board created by Executive Order No. 6859 ... is hereby terminated'.
EO 6771 (June 30, 1934) ordered the National Recovery Review Board discontinued 'prior to July 1, 1934' and that it 'shall cease to exist on that date'.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: Interval: from the order's date to July 1, 1934.

mechanisms.description: EO 7252 (December 21, 1935, effective January 1, 1936) terminated 'The National Recovery Administration and the office of Administrator thereof'.

Single act performed on issue: an appointment or designation of named persons, a dismissal of a complaint, or an order that only amends or revokes another order. The command is exhausted when the order issues; the appointee's tenure, the dismissal's result and the amended text are consequences or evidence for another order's lifecycle.
EO 7076's own operative period: it continued Title I orders and agencies 'until April 1, 1936'.

Express revocation or rescission by a later held order naming the member: EO 7234 (November 25, 1935) revoking EO 2040 and EO 3761; EO 6064 (March 3, 1933) rescinding EO 5143; EO 6344 (October 20, 1933) revoking EO 6223.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: Fixed: the acting order's date, read from its held text.

mechanisms.description: End of the Canal Zone. The Panama Canal Treaty of 1977 entered into force October 1, 1979: it terminated the 1903 Convention (art. I(1)), the Canal Zone Government ceased to operate in Panama (art. III(10)) and Panama reassumed plenary jurisdiction over the former Zone (art. XI(1)). The Panama Canal Act of 1979 continued Zone laws and regulations only 'for the purpose of the exercise by the United States of law enforcement and judicial jurisdiction during the transition period' (sec. 2101) and re-read 'Canal Zone' in surviving laws and regulations as the treaty areas made available to the United States (sec. 3(b)). The Treaty terminated at noon, December 31, 1999 (art. II(2)), the 'Canal Transfer Date' of 22 U.S.C. 3602(d), after which no area answering to 'Canal Zone' remained.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: Interval: from the order's date to December 31, 1999 (outer bound); civil government functions ended October 1, 1979 and transition-period court and police jurisdiction 30 months later, but this doctrine does not date members inside the interval.

mechanisms.description: Philippine independence. Section 10(a) of the Philippine Independence Act directed the President to 'withdraw and surrender all right of possession, supervision, jurisdiction, control, or sovereignty' over the Islands on July 4 after the ten-year Commonwealth period; Proclamation 2695 (July 4, 1946) did so. An order whose operative content is United States supervision of the Islands' government (the Governor General's reporting, the High Commissioner's functions for the Commonwealth) has no object after that date.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: Interval: from the order's date to July 4, 1946 (earlier ends, such as the Commonwealth's inauguration on November 15, 1935, may control and are not dated here).

procedure.description: Expressly revoked by EO 7234 (Nov. 25, 1935): EO 2040 and EO 3761, Canal Zone postal money-order rules.

lead.basis: EO 7234 section 7 names the member and states that it is 'hereby revoked'.

date_rule.basis: date of EO 7234 in its held text

gaps: EO 7234 is held only as an APP mirror transcription.
Deposits outstanding under the revoked rules are accrued consequences, not continued operation; EO 7234's own transition terms were not examined.

procedure.description: Expressly rescinded by EO 6064 (Mar. 3, 1933): EO 5143, passenger restriction from Oriental ports.

lead.basis: EO 6064 names EO 5143 and states that it 'hereby is rescinded'.

date_rule.basis: date of EO 6064 in its held text

gaps: EO 6064 is held as APP and Hathi transcriptions, not an authenticated original.

procedure.description: Expressly revoked by EO 6344 (Oct. 20, 1933): EO 6223, a fund allocation.

lead.basis: EO 6344 states that it 'supersedes Executive Order No. 6223 of July 27, 1933, which is hereby revoked'.

date_rule.basis: date of EO 6344 in its held text

gaps: Any money moved under EO 6223 before revocation is an accrued consequence.

procedure.description: NIRA section 3(e) complaint dismissals: a one-time determination on an import complaint.

when.text_regex: no further action be taken with regard to said complaint|(is|be) (hereby )?dismissed

lead.basis: The order dismisses a single complaint under NIRA section 3(e); the determination is performed when the order issues and commands nothing afterwards. Title I's end (April 1, 1936) is a later event.

gaps: A few dismissals also recite findings about the President's Reemployment Agreement or other programs; the reviewer should confirm no second operative clause.

procedure.description: Orders constituting or staffing the National Industrial Recovery Board (EO 6859, 6993, 7025), terminated by EO 7075.

lead.basis: Each order's operative content creates, reconstitutes or fills the National Industrial Recovery Board; EO 7075 section 1 terminated that Board on June 15, 1935.

gaps: EO 6859 section 3 also lets the Board exercise powers conferred on the Administrator; those powers were re-conferred on the new Administrator by EO 7075 section 2, a new grant, not a continuation of EO 6859.

procedure.description: Orders creating or funding the National Recovery Review Board (EO 6632, 6637), abolished by EO 6771.

when.text_regex: National Recovery Review Board|order dated March 7, 1934

lead.basis: The order's operative content creates or funds the National Recovery Review Board; EO 6771 ordered that Board to cease to exist on July 1, 1934.

gaps: Unspent money allotted by EO 6637 is an accrued consequence; its return was not traced.

procedure.description: EO 7076 itself: continued Title I orders and agencies until April 1, 1936.

lead.basis: The order's only command extends other Title I orders and agencies 'until April 1, 1936'; its own operation ends on that date, which is also the date Title I ceased (NIRA sec. 2(c) as amended).

date_rule.basis: own terms; NIRA sec. 2(c) as amended

gaps: Held only as mirror transcriptions; both say the orders' period was limited to 'June 26, 1935', probably a transcription of 'June 16, 1935'. The discrepancy does not affect the April 1, 1936 end.

procedure.description: Post-June 14, 1935 Title I administration: EO 7075 (office of Administrator, Divisions of Review and Business Cooperation) and EO 7159 (Acting Administrator).

when.text_regex: Administrator of the National Recovery Administration

lead.basis: EO 7252 terminated the NRA and the office of Administrator effective January 1, 1936 and required the transferred divisions' functions to end by April 1, 1936; NIRA sec. 2(c) as amended made every agency established under Title I cease to exist on April 1, 1936. The appointments and the termination of the old Board in EO 7075 are single acts performed on issue.

gaps: The Division of Review's work was later carried on by a committee under the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act of 1935 (EO 7323), a new basis; the doctrine treats it as independent and does not trace it.

procedure.description: Title I orders issued before June 15, 1935 that rest on Title I alone (main NRA branch).

when.text_regex: title I\b|title 1 of|Code of Fair Competition|section 9 ?\(c\)|transportation in interstate and foreign commerce of petroleum|Reemployment Agreement|sections? 2 ?\(b\)|section 10 ?\(a\)

not.text_regex: title II\b|titles I and II|section 20[0-9]|Public,? No\.? 5\b|March 31, 1933|Deficiency Act|Agricultural Adjustment|Federal Emergency Relief|Emergency Appropriation Act|Emergency Relief Appropriation|Public Resolution (No\.? )?44|joint resolution approved June 19, 1934|Reconstruction Finance|Federal Trade Commission Act|act to create a Federal Trade Commission|Code of the District of Columbia|Commodity Credit Corporation|banking corporation|Export-Import Bank|Bituminous Coal Conservation

lead.basis: The order was issued under Title I of NIRA before June 15, 1935 and cites no other statute. EO 7076 amended every such order to continue it only 'until April 1, 1936', and NIRA sec. 2(c) as amended ended Title I and its agencies on that date. Code-dependent commands ended earlier, on June 14, 1935 (S.J. Res. 113 sec. 2); dismissals, denials, appointments and amendments were exhausted on issue. Schechter and Panama Refining are validity notes, not ends.

date_rule.basis: EO 7076; NIRA sec. 2(c) as amended by S.J. Res. 113 sec. 1

gaps: EO 7076 is held only as a mirror transcription.

Orders that cite Title I 'and otherwise' may rest in part on unnamed general authority; EO 7076 still reaches them because they were issued under Title I, but a reviewer should confirm that no clause stands on another statute.
The machine test for 'no other statute' is a text pattern; a statute cited in words the pattern misses would make the member an outlier.

procedure.description: NRA-typed orders whose text is an amendment of another order issued under Title I (EO 6612-A amending EO 6580; EO 6836 amending EO 6770).

when.text_regex: ^(Paragraph numbered \d+ of )?Executive Order No\. ?\d+\S*[^.]{0,160}? is hereby amended

not.text_regex: titles I and II|title II\b|hereby established

lead.basis: The order's only command amends another order; it is spent on issue, and the text it inserted is evidence for the amended order's lifecycle (owner rule in the author brief).

gaps: The inserted text (for example EO 6836's appointment of Donald R. Richberg as Director of the Industrial Emergency Committee) lives or dies with the amended order, whose end is decided elsewhere (EO 6770 is open under O1; EO 6580 is on N6).

procedure.description: Canal Zone appointments or designations of named persons (Isthmian Canal Commission members, Canal Zone justices, special judges).

lead.basis: The order appoints or designates named persons to a Canal Zone office; the appointment is a single act performed when the order issues. A stated term ('until January 1, 1927') or a salary fixed for the appointee limits the appointee's tenure, which is a consequence of the act and ended long before the cutoff in any event.

gaps: Compensation fixed for an appointee runs with the tenure; the end of each tenure (and the discontinuance of the Isthmian Canal Commission under the Panama Canal Act of August 24, 1912, 37 Stat. 560, not held) is not traced.
Some designation texts are ProQuest scans graded archival_replica_scan_pending_codebook; identity must be confirmed by a reader.

procedure.description: Canal Zone orders that only amend or revoke another order (amending a compensation order, revoking a transfer order, correcting a typographical error).

lead.basis: The order's only command amends or revokes another order; it is spent on issue, and the change it made is evidence for the other order's lifecycle (owner rule in the author brief).

gaps: The amended orders' own ends are decided elsewhere.

procedure.description: Canal Zone government orders confined to the Zone, whose whole text is read (Zone courts' jurisdiction, Zone usury rule, Governor's powers within Zone territory and waters).

when.text_regex: for the Canal Zone|Canal Zone Government|courts of the Canal Zone|territory and waters of the Canal Zone

not.text_regex: TRUNCATED|Panama Rail ?road|cities of Panama|city of Panama|Col[oó]n|Republic of Panama|civil[- ]service|Schedule [AB]\b|compensation|salary|annuit|estates?\b|Washington office|office in Washington|appoint

lead.basis: The order's operative content governs the Canal Zone only. The Panama Canal Treaty (in force October 1, 1979) ended the Canal Zone Government and returned plenary jurisdiction to Panama; the Panama Canal Act of 1979 kept Zone laws and regulations in force only for transition-period law enforcement and courts (sec. 2101) and re-read 'Canal Zone' as the treaty areas (sec. 3(b)); the Treaty terminated at noon December 31, 1999, after which no area answering to 'Canal Zone' remained. The order had no object after that date at the latest.

date_rule.basis: Panama Canal Treaty art. II(2); 22 U.S.C. 3602(d)

gaps: The Treaty and 22 U.S.C. 3602(d) are read on the web only and must be acquired.
Earlier ends (supersession by later Zone orders, the Canal Zone Code at 76A Stat. 1, the 1979 Act's amendment of 50 U.S.C. 191 in sec. 3302(a)) are not dated.

procedure.description: Philippine orders on U.S. supervision of the Islands' government (Governor General's reports; High Commissioner's functions for the Commonwealth).

when.text_regex: Governor ?General of the Philippine Islands|High Commissioner to the Commonwealth of the Philippine Islands

lead.basis: The order's operative content is U.S. supervision of the Islands' government. Section 10(a) of the Philippine Independence Act and Proclamation 2695 withdrew and surrendered all U.S. supervision, jurisdiction and control over the Islands on July 4, 1946; the order had no object after that date at the latest.

gaps: Earlier ends (the Governor General's office ended with the Commonwealth's inauguration on November 15, 1935; the Bureau of Insular Affairs moved to Interior under Reorganization Plan No. II of 1939) are not dated and their sources are not held.
EO 2456: the held text is signed September 19, 1916, the claim says September 16, 1916; settle identity from an official printing.

EO 7447 also authorizes U.S. diplomats and consuls abroad to act on Commonwealth extradition requests; that authority existed only for the Commonwealth and falls with it, but a reviewer should confirm.

procedure.description: NRA-typed orders that rest on another statute or authority (Title II public works, appropriation acts, Public Resolution 44, corporation charters, the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act), or post-June 14, 1935 orders not reached by EO 7076.

lead.basis: Neither EO 7076 nor NIRA sec. 2(c) reaches these orders by their terms: they rest wholly or partly on another statute, cite no Title I power, have no held text, or were issued after June 14, 1935 with a function that outlived April 1, 1936.

gaps: Each needs its own statute's lifecycle (Title II and its extensions; the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act of 1935; Public Resolution 44, 48 Stat. 1183; the Commodity Credit Corporation and Export-Import Bank statutes) or the PD-ADMIN fund-allotment and organization rules.

procedure.description: Canal Zone orders not decided: content reaching outside the Zone, Panama Railroad corporate matters, continuing individual rights, general civil-service rules, truncated or unidentified texts.

lead.basis: The class event ends Zone-only government, but these orders reach outside the Zone (Panama City and Colon harbors, Washington offices, general U.S. civil-service rules), rest on Panama Railroad corporate arrangements, create continuing individual rights (injury compensation, estates, deposits), or their held text is cut off, scanned unreadably or another order's.

gaps: Full official texts for truncated orders (Panama Canal Record or the 1911 GPO compilation); later-law sources for each outlier (Hull-Alfaro Treaty of 1936 for Panama and Colon sanitation; 37 Stat. 560 for the Isthmian Canal Commission's discontinuance; Civil Service Rules history for schedule amendments).

procedure.description: Catch-all: Philippine-typed orders with no Philippine subject and anything else.

lead.basis: The order's own text does not concern U.S. government of the Philippine Islands (for example Alien Property Custodian delegations, foreign-built ship registry, a general order on federal law officers), so Philippine independence is not shown to reach it.

gaps: Route to the family that fits the order's real subject (PD-WAR-EMERGENCY for Alien Property Custodian orders; PD-ADMIN for general organization orders).

undecidable.reason: NRA-typed orders resting on statutes other than NIRA Title I (Title II, appropriation acts, Public Resolution 44, corporation charters, Emergency Relief Appropriation Act) or on no named Title I power
Post-June 14, 1935 Title I orders whose function outlived April 1, 1936 or that rest only on the Title's expiry (EO 7120, 7192, 7252)
NRA orders with no held text (EO 6786-A, 7010-P)

Canal Zone orders reaching outside the Zone, resting on Panama Railroad corporate matters, creating continuing individual rights, amending general civil-service rules, or held only in truncated, scanned or mismatched text
Philippine-typed orders with no Philippine subject
